_doc: Skips CI accepts, per platform. scripts/ci_report.py fails a job on any other skip. 'reason' must equal the pytest skip reason exactly; use 'reason_prefix' only for reasons that embed measured values. 'why' says why the skip is legitimate. Add an entry only together with a test that covers the same behaviour where it can run.

all.reason: bundled renderer is not executable on this platform
all.why: the bundled LibreOffice only exists inside a built macOS app
CI engine jobs do not build the macOS app
CI engine jobs do not build the macOS app

all.reason: speed gate skipped because CI is set: the >=1.5x threshold is machine-dependent (acceptance contract allows this skip on CI, and it is NOT a pass). Run on a quiet machine: python scripts/verify_shard.py --mode speed --perf on
all.why: shared runners are too noisy for a speed threshold; equivalence is still asserted

linux.reason: Windows-only: asserts the CI runner finds the LibreOffice its job installed
Job Objects exist only on Windows; POSIX uses process groups. This skip is printed, not silent - the grandchild assertions above still run on POSIX.
Job Object handles exist only on Windows; POSIX uses process groups. This skip is printed, not silent - the grandchild assertions above still run on POSIX.

macos.why: hosted macOS runners have one writable filesystem

macos.reason: Windows-only: asserts the CI runner finds the LibreOffice its job installed
Job Objects exist only on Windows; POSIX uses process groups. This skip is printed, not silent - the grandchild assertions above still run on POSIX.
Job Object handles exist only on Windows; POSIX uses process groups. This skip is printed, not silent - the grandchild assertions above still run on POSIX.

windows.why: hosted Windows runners have no second volume the test can create
Windows has no SIGINT/SIGTERM delivery to a child; cancellation is covered by the complete-run gates

windows.reason: a read-only cache directory cannot be enforced on Windows or when running as root
windows.why: Windows ACLs differ from POSIX modes

windows.reason: POSIX-only signals/process-group/ps (SIGINT, SIGKILL, os.killpg, ps); Windows CI runs the complete-run gates

windows.reason_prefix: cannot create a symlink on this Windows runner
windows.why: the test tries to create the symlink first and only skips when Windows refuses it (SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege is not granted on hosted runners); the refusal text is printed in the skip reason, so the premise is observed on every run. The same path-containment check runs on Linux and macOS
